outcome: The general Halperin conjecture (collapse at E2 of the rational Serre spectral sequence for every orientable fibration with a positively elliptic fibre) is open in every source I could read, and no event since 26 January 2024 settles it. The only in-window movements are a 2026 Chen–Yau refinement of a special algebraic case (a degree bound independent of the number of variables, for moduli algebras of hypersurface singularities) and a 2025 KTH master's survey that claims no new case. No AI system was found involved in any event.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone. (P1) Scope: orientable fibrations F → E → B over a simply connected base (Wikipedia's wording) whose fibre F is rationally elliptic with nonzero Euler characteristic. The literature narrows this to positively elliptic (F0) fibres, meaning finite-dimensional rational cohomology concentrated in even degrees; Markl's 1989 version uses 1-connected rationally elliptic fibres with H*(F;Q) zero in odd degrees. The Wikipedia wording 'nonzero' is looser than the literature's 'positive'. (P2) Claim: the rational Serre spectral sequence of every such fibration collapses at E2. The literature states this as equivalent to every such fibration being totally non-cohomologous to zero (TNCZ): H*(E;Q) → H*(F;Q) is surjective, and π1(B) acts trivially on H*(F;Q). (P3) Algebraic form, by Meier (1982): for an F0 fibre, the conjecture holds exactly when its rational cohomology algebra has no nontrivial derivation of negative degree. Thomas (1981) gives a further equivalence, TNCZ ⇔ pure fibration. The statement asks for all such fibrations over all simply connected bases, with no restriction on fibre formal dimension or type. Partial results restrict one of these; none removes the restriction.

events.what_happened: Jean-Claude Thomas, 'Rational homotopy of Serre fibrations', Annales de l'Institut Fourier 31(3) (1981) 71–90. The abstract (opened) introduces pure fibrations in rational homotopy theory and does not mention Halperin's conjecture. The claims below are second-hand, from Lupton's 2000 arXiv paper as read in search snippets: for a positively elliptic fibre, TNCZ is equivalent to the fibration being pure, and the conjecture holds when the minimal model of F has dim V^even = 1 or 2. Lu's extension to dim V^even = 3 is named there but not read.
events.delivers: Second-hand: for positively elliptic fibres whose minimal model has dim V^even ≤ 2, Halperin's conjecture holds, so every fibration with that fibre is TNCZ and the Serre spectral sequence collapses at E2. Restricted to that model class.
events.remains: Positively elliptic fibres with dim V^even ≥ 3 (dim V^even = 3 is claimed by Lu, not read) and the general case.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: positive partial result for a model class.

events.what_happened: W. Meier, 'Rational universal fibrations and flag manifolds', Mathematische Annalen 258 (1982) 329–340 (DOI 10.1007/BF01450686). Not opened. Second-hand, from the Kennard–Wu abstract and search snippets: reformulates the conjecture algebraically (for an F0-space, no nontrivial derivation of negative degree on the rational cohomology algebra); links it to the rational homotopy type of the universal fibration; proves the conjecture for flag manifolds G/T with T a maximal torus.
events.delivers: Second-hand: a fibre-level equivalence, Halperin's conjecture for an F0-space ⇔ no negative-degree derivations on its cohomology algebra; and the conjecture for flag manifolds G/T.
events.remains: Positively elliptic fibres in general. The paper supplies the reformulation and the flag-manifold case.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture (equivalence and special case).

events.what_happened: H. Shiga and M. Tezuka, 'Rational fibrations, homogeneous spaces with positive Euler characteristics and Jacobians', Annales de l'Institut Fourier 37(1) (1987) 81–106. Abstract (opened): an orientable fibration whose fibre has the homotopy type of G/U with rank G = rank U is totally non-homologous to zero for rational coefficients; the Jacobian of Weyl-invariant polynomials is central. Halperin appears only in the bibliography. Later surveys (second-hand) count the equal-rank homogeneous case as verified for Halperin's conjecture.
events.delivers: For fibrations whose fibre is a homogeneous space G/U with rank U = rank G: the fibration is totally non-homologous to zero over Q, so the rational Serre spectral sequence collapses in that sense. The paper is not stated to address the conjecture; the link is second-hand. Whether the homology version it proves is equivalent to the cohomology TNCZ form of the conjecture is not established here.
events.remains: Positively elliptic fibres that are not equal-rank homogeneous spaces, and the general case.

checked_by.who: Annales de l'Institut Fourier (journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; referees not named in the sources read

events.direction: Toward the conjecture: verified for the equal-rank homogeneous fibres (in the homology sense).

events.what_happened: Akinori Matsui and Hajime Sato, 'Stiefel-Whitney homology classes and homotopy type of Euler spaces', Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan 37(3) (1985). The full PDF was unreadable to the fetcher. Second-hand from a search snippet of the introduction: 'As a byproduct, they obtain counterexamples to Halperin's conjecture (Fulton-MacPherson [4])'. The setting is Euler spaces (Halperin–Toledo), not rational elliptic fibrations.
events.delivers: Per the introduction sentence (second-hand): counterexamples to 'Halperin's conjecture as stated by Fulton and MacPherson', in the Euler-space formulation. Whether that formulation is the rational-fibration conjecture of the bullet is not established.
events.remains: Unknown from what I could read: the relation between the Euler-space formulation and the fibration statement is unresolved.
events.doubts: The counterexamples are not described in anything I could read, and the Fulton–MacPherson source was not located. Whether the same conjecture is meant is open.
events.direction: Against 'Halperin's conjecture' if the Euler-space formulation is the same statement; the formulations are not reconciled.
events.object: Not described in the sources read. The introduction says only that counterexamples come out of a construction of Euler spaces with prescribed Stiefel–Whitney homology classes.

events.what_happened: Martin Markl, 'Towards one conjecture on collapsing of the Serre spectral sequence', Proceedings of the Winter School 'Geometry and Physics' (Srní 1989; Palermo 1990, pp. 151–159). The abstract (opened) restates the conjecture for a 1-connected rationally elliptic fibre F with H*(F;k) zero in odd degrees (char 0): every fibration F → E → B is TNCZ. It proves this under one of three extra hypotheses: (i) the Lie algebra cohomology H*(C*(π*(ΩF)⊗Q)) is finite dimensional; (ii) F is rationally coformal; (iii) H*(F;k) has a presentation k[x1..xn]/(f1..fm) with a condition whose text is cut off in the readable abstract.
events.delivers: For fibres satisfying one of (i), (ii) or (iii): every fibration with that fibre is TNCZ, so the Serre spectral sequence collapses at E2. The abstract gives no unconditional case.
events.remains: Fibres satisfying none of the three extra hypotheses; the general conjecture.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: conditional proof under three hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Gregory Lupton, 'Variations on a conjecture of Halperin', Banach Center Publications 45 (1998) 115–135 (Homotopy and Geometry); arXiv:math/0010124, first posted 12 Oct 2000 (the only version listed). The arXiv abstract page (opened) says: Halperin conjectured that the Serre spectral sequence of certain fibrations with elliptic fibre collapses at E2; Lupton rephrases this via formality relations between base and total spaces, relates numerical invariants, and proves some weakened forms (Remark 4.4, Corollary 4.5, Theorem 4.7 in the paper; not readable). The statements of the weakened forms were not read.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 12 Oct 2000 (only version); journal volume 1998.
events.delivers: Weakened forms of the conjecture; the paper's own framing is that these are weak versions, not the conjecture. Exact statements not read.
events.remains: The conjecture in the form stated.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: weakened forms and a reformulation.

events.what_happened: Toshihiro Yamaguchi, 'An example of a fiber in fibrations whose Serre spectral sequences collapse', Czechoslovak Mathematical Journal 55(4) (2005) 997–1001. Abstract (opened, segments): constructs a space X such that every orientable fibration with fibre X is rationally totally non-cohomologous to zero, while H*(X;Q) has a nontrivial derivation of negative degree. The page does not mention Halperin's conjecture. A search summary says X has Euler characteristic zero; I did not verify this against the paper, whose PDF was unreadable.
events.delivers: A space X for which the TNCZ conclusion holds for all fibrations with fibre X although H*(X;Q) has a negative-degree derivation. Per the unverified search summary, X has Euler characteristic zero, which places it outside the positive-Euler-characteristic hypothesis, so the example would not contradict the conjecture as stated.
events.remains: Nothing in the conjecture's positive-Euler-characteristic hypothesis is touched, if the Euler characteristic claim holds.
events.doubts: The Euler characteristic claim is from a search summary, not from the paper. Whether the example is elliptic is not stated in the abstract.
events.direction: Against the 'negative derivation ⇒ no TNCZ' reading of the algebraic form in general; not against the positive-Euler-characteristic case if the χ = 0 claim holds.
events.object: A space X (not named in the abstract) with every orientable fibration with fibre X TNCZ and a nontrivial negative-degree derivation on H*(X;Q). The construction is not described in what I could read.

events.what_happened: Manuel Amann and Lee Kennard, 'Positive curvature and rational ellipticity', arXiv:1403.1440 (first submitted 6 Mar 2014), Algebraic & Geometric Topology 15 (2015) 2269–2301. Abstract (opened): combines positive curvature with rational ellipticity; gives 'confirmations of famous conjectures by Hopf and Halperin under additional torus symmetry'.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 6 Mar 2014; journal version AGT 2015 (the arXiv title differs from the journal title per a search summary).
events.delivers: Halperin's conjecture confirmed in the setting of simply connected, rationally elliptic, positively curved manifolds with additional torus symmetry (the abstract's wording; the precise hypotheses were not read).
events.remains: The conjecture for fibres and spaces without positive curvature and large torus symmetry, and in general.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; referees not named in the sources read
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper in 2015

events.direction: Toward the conjecture: confirmation in a symmetric positively curved setting.

events.what_happened: Manuel Amann and Lee Kennard, 'Positive curvature and torus symmetry in small dimensions, I — Dimensions 10, 12, 14, and 16', arXiv:1512.01302 (first submitted 4 Dec 2015). Abstract (opened): studies invariants of manifolds with positive sectional curvature and large torus symmetry in even dimensions up to 16, and studies positively elliptic manifolds. The one sentence on Halperin: 'we prove the Halperin conjecture in this context for dimensions up to 16 or Euler characteristics up to 16'. A search summary gives the journal version as Comm. Contemp. Math. 22(6) (2019), article 1950053, titled 'Positive curvature and symmetry in small dimensions'; not opened.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 4 Dec 2015; journal version Comm. Contemp. Math. 2019 per a search summary (not opened).
events.delivers: Halperin's conjecture for positively elliptic manifolds in the paper's torus-symmetry setting, for formal dimension up to 16 or Euler characteristic up to 16 (the abstract's wording).
events.remains: Such manifolds of larger formal dimension or Euler characteristic, and the conjecture for general fibres.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; referees not named in the sources read
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the second-stage paper in 2019 (per a search summary; not opened)

events.direction: Toward the conjecture: confirmation for a restricted class of manifolds in low dimension / low Euler characteristic.

events.what_happened: Hao Chen, Stephen S.-T. Yau, Huaiqing Zuo, 'Non-existence of negative weight derivations on positively graded Artinian algebras', Transactions of the AMS 372(4) (2019) 2493–2535. The AMS page was blocked (HTTP 403). Read via the Tsinghua archive page: for positively graded Artinian algebras C[x1..xn]/(f1..fm), no negative-weight derivations when the degrees of the f_j are at least a constant depending only on the variable weights, with sharper bounds in special cases. 'Halperin Conjecture' appears in the keyword list, not in the abstract. The 2026 Chen–Yau abstract calls this the earlier result it refines.
events.revisions: No arXiv posting located; an earlier public date is possible, because the 2016 Fudan talk claims these results (see fudan-2016).
events.delivers: Algebraic form of Halperin's conjecture for positively graded Artinian algebras C[x]/(f) whose relation degrees exceed a bound depending only on the variable weights ('relations of large degree', from a secondary list). Not established from what I read that these algebras are exactly the F0 cohomology algebras of positively elliptic fibres (even weights), nor that the paper contains the fibre-level collapse statement.
events.remains: Relations of degree below the bound; the general case; and the fibre-level Conjecture I of the 2016 talk, unless the paper contains it.

checked_by.who: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society (journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; referees not named in the sources read
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper in 2019

events.doubts: Whether the paper proves the fibre-level collapse that the 2016 talk called Conjecture I, or only the algebraic Conjecture II, is not established. A search summary names Chen and Qiu Chengdong as authors in a Jinan University news item; this conflicts with the Tsinghua listing and is not resolved.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture (vanishing of negative-weight derivations) for the stated degree range.

events.what_happened: Talk by Stephen S.-T. Yau with Hao Chen and Huaiqing Zuo, 'Negative Weight Derivation and Rational Homotopy Theory', Fudan University, 27 May 2016 (event-page abstract, opened). It says Halperin proposed his conjecture in spring 1976 in the Lille rational homotopy seminar, and that the problem 'remains open'. The talk formulates two conjectures: Conjecture I, collapse of the Serre spectral sequence for fibrations whose fibre is a finite-dimensional commutative positively graded algebra C[x1..xn]/(f1..fm) with positive even weights and large relation degrees; Conjecture II, vanishing of negative-weight derivations for such algebras, which implies Conjecture I. It then says: 'We prove recently that Conjectures I and II are true.' No written proof was located.
events.revisions: No written version located. The talk date is 27 May 2016; the write-up date is unknown, so 2016 is the only date I can give.
events.delivers: Claimed in the abstract only, and unverified: Conjecture I (a generalisation of the fibre-level statement) and Conjecture II (algebraic) for the stated algebra class. A search summary describes Conjecture I as dropping the requirement that the fibre be elliptic with positive Euler characteristic; not checked against the abstract text.
events.doubts: A claim in a talk abstract with no written proof found. The nearest published paper, Chen–Yau–Zuo 2019, is not confirmed to contain Conjecture I. The 2026 Chen–Yau abstract does not repeat the claim.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, if the claimed proofs hold.

events.what_happened: Lee Kennard and Yantao Wu, 'Halperin's conjecture in formal dimensions up to 20', arXiv:2104.04086 (v1, 8 Apr 2021, the only version listed); Communications in Algebra 51(8) (2023) 3606–3622, DOI 10.1080/00927872.2023.2186705 (the NSF record gives publication 3 Aug 2023; the publisher page was blocked). Abstract (opened): 'A 1976 conjecture of Halperin on positively elliptic spaces was recently confirmed in formal dimensions up to 16. In this article, we shorten the proof and extend the result up to formal dimension 20.' The proof uses Meier's algebraic characterisation, so it involves only polynomial algebras, ideals and derivations.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 8 Apr 2021 (only version listed); journal version 2023 (NSF record: 3 Aug 2023).
events.delivers: Halperin's conjecture for positively elliptic (F0) spaces in every formal dimension ≤ 20. By Meier's equivalence, the conjecture for an F0 fibre is an algebraic property of its cohomology, so this covers every positively elliptic fibre of formal dimension ≤ 20, and hence (via the TNCZ equivalence) the fibrations with such fibres. The exact theorem wording was not read.
events.remains: Positively elliptic fibres of formal dimension > 20, and the conjecture in general.

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; referees not named in the sources read
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper in 2023 (NSF record: published 3 Aug 2023)

events.doubts: Full text unread: the arXiv PDF and a Syracuse PDF were not readable, so the theorem statement and the acknowledgements were not checked. Whether any step is a computer check (the abstract calls the proof elementary) is not established.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture: no negative derivations, hence TNCZ, for F0 fibres of formal dimension ≤ 20.

events.what_happened: Wágner Badilla-Céspedes, Abel Castorena, Daniel Duarte, 'Higher Jacobian matrix of weighted homogeneous polynomials and derivation algebras', arXiv:2312.04677 (v1 7 Dec 2023; v2 24 Jul 2025). Abstract (opened): the ideal of maximal minors of the higher-order Jacobian matrix of a weighted homogeneous polynomial is weighted homogeneous; as an application, a partial answer to a conjecture on non-existence of negative weight derivations on the higher Nash blowup local algebra of a hypersurface. Halperin and elliptic spaces are not mentioned.
events.delivers: A partial answer to a non-existence conjecture for negative weight derivations on higher Nash blowup algebras of hypersurfaces. This is a different algebra and conjecture from Halperin's.
events.direction: Not about the conjecture: neighbouring question on negative weight derivations.

events.what_happened: Jorge Martín, master's thesis 'The Halperin conjecture' (mathematics, KTH Royal Institute of Technology), defended Friday 29 Aug 2025, 13:30, on Zoom; supervisor Alexander Berglund (KTH calendar, opened). The announcement calls it 'a long-standing open problem in algebraic topology': the rational Serre spectral sequence of orientable fibrations whose fibre is positively elliptic degenerates at E2. The thesis surveys background, alternative formulations and the current state of research; it states two rephrasings and shows their equivalence with the original; and it ends with counterexamples showing the statement is sharp (per the announcement). A Stockholm University calendar lists the same talk as Master's thesis M9 (search snippet, not opened). The full text was not found; a DiVA search returned nothing.
events.revisions: None known. The text may be posted on DiVA later; the posting date is not established.
events.delivers: Per the announcement only: a survey; the equivalence of the conjecture with two reformulations, with proofs; counterexamples to a related or sharpened statement (not described). No new case of the conjecture is claimed in the announcement.
events.remains: The conjecture as stated, in general.

checked_by.qualification: Named supervisor in the KTH calendar; expertise in rational homotopy theory is my general knowledge, not checked in the sources read
checked_by.what_they_did: Named as supervisor. Whether he examined or approved the thesis is not established.

events.doubts: Full text unread; the counterexamples are described only as showing that the statement is sharp, so they may concern variants (for example fibres with Euler characteristic zero) rather than the conjecture itself. Not established.
events.direction: Survey: no direction stated for the conjecture.
events.object: Counterexamples said to show the statement is sharp. Not described in the announcement; I could not locate the thesis text.

events.what_happened: Wágner Badilla-Céspedes, Abel Castorena, Daniel Duarte, Luis Núñez-Betancourt, 'Non-existence of negative derivations on the higher Nash blowup local algebra', arXiv:2508.14353 (v1 20 Aug 2025). Abstract (opened): for a weighted homogeneous polynomial f with an isolated singularity, the higher Nash blowup local algebra T_n(f) admits no negative weighted derivations for n ≥ 2. This answers affirmatively a conjecture of Hussain–Ma–Yau–Zuo. Halperin, elliptic spaces and the Serre spectral sequence are not mentioned.
events.delivers: Non-existence of negative weighted derivations on the higher Nash blowup algebra T_n(f), n ≥ 2, for weighted homogeneous isolated singularities. A different algebra and conjecture.
events.direction: Not about the conjecture: neighbouring question on negative weight derivations.

events.what_happened: Bingyi Chen and Stephen S.-T. Yau, 'On nonexistence of negative weight derivations on moduli algebras: Yau's conjecture', Matematicheskii Sbornik 217(1) (2026) 114–138. The journal page (opened via the redirect to journals.rcsi.science) gives the abstract in summary and quotes two sentences: Halperin 'proposed a famous conjecture', and the conjecture 'implies the collapsing of the Serre spectral sequence' for certain fibrations. The authors consider graded complete intersection Artinian algebras over characteristic zero. In the special case where the defining equations are the partial derivatives of one polynomial (a moduli algebra of a hypersurface singularity), they prove a version with a bound independent of the number of variables, refining Chen–Yau–Zuo 2019. A Tsinghua preprint with the same title exists. Journal dates from a search summary (not opened, because Math-Net was unreachable): received 20 Sep 2024, revised 22 Apr 2025. The preprint posting date is not established. The date field is the journal receipt year, and is a proxy, not a public date.
events.revisions: Journal revision 22 Apr 2025 per a search summary (not opened). Tsinghua preprint version and date not established.
events.delivers: For the special case f_i = ∂f/∂x_i (moduli algebras of weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularities), with graded complete intersection Artinian algebras over characteristic zero: no negative-weight derivations, with a degree bound independent of the number of variables. Whether these algebras meet the even-weight (F0) hypotheses of Halperin's conjecture is not established from the abstract. The paper treats the conjecture as something that 'would imply' the vanishing; it does not claim to prove Halperin's conjecture.
events.remains: Halperin's conjecture in general; Yau's conjecture for general moduli algebras; the general graded complete intersection case outside the partial-derivative special case and the degree bound.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2026 (per journal record)

disputes.summary: The 2016 Fudan talk abstract claims Yau, Chen and Zuo proved Conjectures I and II, with Conjecture I generalising Halperin's fibre-level statement. The nearest published paper, Chen–Yau–Zuo (Trans. AMS 2019), is confirmed to contain the algebraic degree-bounded vanishing; it is not confirmed to contain the fibre-level Conjecture I. The 2026 Chen–Yau abstract describes the 2019 result as an earlier result it refines, and calls Halperin's conjecture a conjecture. Not resolved.

Matsui and Sato (1985) state, per a search snippet of their introduction, that they obtain counterexamples to 'Halperin's conjecture' as stated by Fulton and MacPherson, in an Euler-space setting. The rational-fibration conjecture of the bullet is a different setting. Whether the two are the same statement is unresolved; I did not read the paper.

Wikipedia's statement uses 'fibre rationally elliptic with nonzero Euler characteristic'. The literature (Markl; Thomas; Meier; Kennard–Wu) uses 'positively elliptic' / F0 (even-graded cohomology), or 'elliptic with even cohomology'. Markl's version also assumes 1-connected fibres. These are close but not identical scopes, and the bullet's wording follows Wikipedia.
The conjecture's origin is given as spring 1976 at the Lille rational homotopy seminar (Fudan 2016 abstract), and as 1977 in one search summary. Minor, unresolved.

The toral rank conjecture (S. Halperin, 1985; also the Halperin–Carlsson conjecture) is a different open problem with the same namesake. It is not the bullet's statement. Its literature (for example Jessup–Lupton arXiv:math/0309434; Ustinovskii arXiv:1203.3685; the counter-examples to a generalised toral rank conjecture arXiv:2011.13411; Amann–Zoller arXiv:1910.04746) was seen in search only, and none of it is dated in the window. Not collected in full.

summary: The general Halperin conjecture is open in every source I could read. Wikipedia (current page, opened) says 'As of 2019, Halperin's conjecture is still open'. A master's thesis defended at KTH on 29 Aug 2025 (announcement opened; full text not found) calls it 'a long-standing open problem'. The Chen–Yau 2026 abstract (opened via the journal page) discusses the conjecture as one whose truth 'would imply' vanishing of negative-weight derivations and collapse of the Serre spectral sequence, and proves only a special case. The partial results, in date order, are: Thomas 1981 (dim V^even ≤ 2; second-hand); Meier 1982 (algebraic reformulation and flag manifolds; second-hand); Shiga–Tezuka 1987 (equal-rank homogeneous fibres, read in the abstract); Markl 1989 (conditional on three hypotheses, read in the abstract); Lupton 1998/2000 (weakened forms, statements not read); Amann–Kennard 2014 and 2015 (positively curved and positively elliptic manifolds under symmetry, read in the abstracts); Chen–Yau–Zuo 2019 (degree-bounded algebraic vanishing, read in the metadata and summary; the AMS page was blocked); and Kennard–Wu 2021 (formal dimension ≤ 20, read in the abstract; full text unreadable). Events in the window since 26 Jan 2024 are: the KTH thesis (defended 29 Aug 2025; announcement only); the Badilla-Céspedes et al. arXiv 2508.14353 (Aug 2025; a different algebra, no Halperin mention); and the Chen–Yau 2026 paper. The Chen–Yau 2026 paper is the one close call. Its special case (partial-derivative relations, degree bound independent of the number of variables) is a real refinement of the algebraic side of the conjecture. But the abstract presents it as a result on Yau's moduli-algebra conjecture, and the conjecture applies to F0 algebras (even weights), which the abstract does not confirm for this case. Its journal receipt date (20 Sep 2024) is the only date I have, and the preprint posting date is not established, so I cannot say whether its first public written argument falls inside the window. Other close calls: whether Kennard–Wu's formal-dimension bound counts as a restricted case of the fibration-level statement (I read Meier's equivalence as yes, which makes it a case of the conjecture for fibres of formal dimension ≤ 20, but I did not read Kennard–Wu's theorem statement to confirm it); whether the 2016 Fudan talk's claimed proofs (Conjectures I and II) are the 2019 paper (unconfirmed, and no written proof located); and whether Matsui–Sato's Euler-space counterexamples bear on the fibration statement (unresolved). Yamaguchi 2005's example would not touch the positive-Euler-characteristic case if its Euler characteristic is zero, as one search summary says; I did not verify that. AI search: I ran more than ten AI-directed queries (AlphaProof, AlphaEvolve, Aristotle, Gemini Deep Think, GPT/OpenAI, Claude/Anthropic, AI-assisted 2026 papers, Lean/formal-conjectures, erdosproblems/Open Problem Garden, and 'AI solved open problem algebraic topology'). None returned a Halperin-specific AI event. The AI results that came up (Erdős unit distance, the Hodge result for CM abelian varieties, the percolation proof, FirstProof, Kourovka, the Georgiev–Gómez-Serrano–Tao–Wagner AlphaEvolve paper) concern other problems. ai.none_found is true for each event because no AI system is named in the sources I read, but for the 2021 Kennard–Wu paper, the 2026 Chen–Yau paper and the 2025 thesis, the full text (including acknowledgements) was unreadable or not found, so the AI answer for those rests on abstracts and metadata. Search-engine summaries were used only to locate sources; each second-hand claim is labelled as such.
competing_reading: Read the Chen–Yau 2026 result as a restricted case of Halperin's conjecture that moves in the window. The algebras are complete intersection Artinian algebras, the conjecture's algebraic form (Meier) is about exactly such algebras, and the result gives vanishing of negative-weight derivations with a bound that no longer depends on the number of variables. Read it as an analogue, not a case, in the other direction: the paper is titled and framed as Yau's moduli-algebra conjecture, the abstract treats Halperin's conjecture as something that 'would imply' the vanishing rather than as the thing proved, and the even-weight (F0) hypothesis is not shown to hold for the partial-derivative case.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Chen–Yau 2026 and of the Tsinghua preprint: the preprint's posting date (for the in-window test), the grading hypotheses (even weights or not), and whether the paper states the link to Halperin's fibration statement. (2) The Martín thesis full text on DiVA, to see whether it contains any new case or only the equivalences and counterexamples. (3) The full text of Kennard–Wu: the theorem statement for fibres of formal dimension ≤ 20, the acknowledgements, and any computer assistance. (4) A written proof of the Fudan 2016 Conjectures I and II, or a statement that Chen–Yau–Zuo 2019 contains Conjecture I. (5) The Matsui–Sato introduction and the Fulton–MacPherson reference, to see whether the Euler-space 'Halperin's conjecture' is the same statement. (6) Any post-2026 arXiv posting titled with 'Halperin conjecture' or 'positively elliptic'.

judgement.why: Pre-snapshot restrictions of the fibre class (Thomas, Meier flag manifolds, Shiga–Tezuka equal-rank, Markl's hypothesis classes, Amann–Kennard, Chen–Yau–Zuo, Kennard–Wu formal dimension ≤ 20) are cases; journal acceptance counts as digestion, Markl's proceedings and the Fudan talk do not. Lupton's weakened forms, Yamaguchi's χ=0 example, Matsui–Sato's Euler-space statement and the Badilla-Céspedes papers on Nash blowup algebras are variants. In the window: the KTH thesis is a survey (none); Chen–Yau 2026 is framed as Yau's moduli-algebra conjecture, with the even-weight F0 hypothesis not shown, so I read it as a variant rather than a case. Its only date is a 2024 journal receipt year, which cannot be placed against 26 January 2024, so after_snapshot is null.
judgement.doubts: Chen–Yau 2026 is the close call: if its algebras are F0 cohomology algebras, it would be a case of the algebraic (Meier) form, but its date is still unplaceable. Several pre-snapshot results (Thomas, Meier) are second-hand. AI answers for Kennard–Wu, Chen–Yau 2026 and the thesis rest on abstracts only.
